items.title: 54270_Doc Cheatham oral history interview
items.q: And that's when you joined Teddy Wilson. That's right.

ctx.x: With Teddy Wilson -- Teddy Wilson just had something altogether different from any band at that time. Style of swing.

items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: Doc Cheatham later came with me when I had three trumpets

ctx.x: He was really good, too. I lost track of him. I heard after my band broke up he went with Kenton for a while and then after that nobody knows what happened to him. And of course, Doc Cheatham later came with me when I had three trumpets, after he left Cab.
So I really had a trumpet section. Every man could play first trumpet and every guy could be a soloist, too.

items.title: Doc Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, New York City, New York, July 28, 1995
items.q: performing with the big bands of Cab Calloway, Teddy Wilson, Benny Carter and Chick Webb.

ctx.x: Doc Cheatham’s remarkable career in jazz reads like a fairy tale. Born Aldolphus Cheatham in 1905, he grew up in Nashville and took up the sax and trumpet at an early age. His first playing experience was at the Bijou Theater where he played behind Bessie Smith, later recording on the soprano sax with another blues great, Ma Rainey.
